raw_response:
**My reasoning:**

I've been farming this land for over 40 years. My two sons work in Handan city now, so it's mostly me and my wife. We have 10 mu of contracted land — good flat ground on the North China Plain, same as everyone else in the village.

I'm not changing what I grow. Wheat and corn, that's the rotation. Every household here does it. The government subsidizes wheat, the cooperative buys it at guaranteed price, and I know these crops. My father grew them, I grew them, and I know what they need season by season. I'm 62 — this is not the time to experiment.

I'll plant 9 mu in the wheat-corn double crop. After wheat harvest in June I'll get the corn in fast — direct seeded, no tilling, save time and fuel. The remaining 1 mu near the house I'll keep for garlic. We eat it, sell some to neighbors. It doesn't need much attention once it's in the ground in October.

For wheat seed I'll buy the improved variety from the township station again — probably Jimai 22 or whatever they recommend this year. For corn I'll use hybrid seed, same brand as last year, gave me 560 jin per mu, which was decent. Traditional seed doesn't yield enough anymore, not worth it.

Fertilizer: I put down compound fertilizer as base when I sow the wheat, then urea at jointing stage. My neighbor says I should cut back on nitrogen but I've seen what happens when you go light — the ears are thin. I'll keep my usual amount. For corn I side-dress urea at the big bell stage.

Irrigation is the real cost here — electricity for the pump. But Quzhou is dry. Wheat needs water at winterization, jointing, heading, and grain filling — four times minimum. Corn gets summer rain mostly, but I'll pump once at silking if it looks dry.

Pesticide: spray herbicide in spring on the wheat, fungicide before heading to protect against scab, and watch for aphids. For corn, herbicide right after seeding, and one more spray if I see borer damage.
